# Micro-test design: `changelog-entry` step 2 wording

Status: design only. Nothing has been run.

## Question

Does the proposed step 2 produce entries that name what the reader can now do or no longer suffers,
without losing the 100-character, one-line limit? And does it do better than the old step 2?

Old: `2. Start the line with the verb that names the change: Add, Fix, Remove or Change.`
New: `2. Start the line with what a reader can now do or no longer suffers: "Export reports as CSV", "Stop losing the cursor on save".`

## Failure type

The baseline (old line skipped in 7 of 10 runs) and the proposal's stated problem ("Fix handler",
"Change parser") are both about the shape of the output, not about breaking a rule under pressure.
The new line is already a recipe (it states what the entry starts with), so the test checks the
recipe's wording. It does not need a pressure scenario or a rationalization table.

## Arms

| Arm | System prompt | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| C: control | The skill with step 2 deleted (steps renumbered). | Shows whether the failure exists without any step 2 guidance. If the control already writes good entries, stop: there is nothing to fix. |
| O: old | The full skill as it is now. | Re-baseline on the same tasks and scoring as the new arm. |
| N: new | The full skill with the proposed step 2. | The thing under test. |

Arm O is re-run, not reused. The old 10-run baseline was scored on different tasks, and I don't
have its prompts or scoring in `specs/`. If they exist elsewhere, tell me and I'll check that arm O
can reuse them.

The system prompt is the whole SKILL.md, because the wording will live there. Do not test the line in isolation.

## Tasks (user message)

Each task gives a merged PR (title, short description, a few changed files) and asks for the
`CHANGELOG.md` entry. Each is built to tempt an internal-part entry:

1. Bug fix with an internal title: "TKT-412: null check in saveHandler.ts". The user-visible effect is that the cursor no longer jumps on save.
2. New capability buried in a refactor-sounding title: "Parser: add csv serializer". The user-visible effect is that reports can be exported as CSV.
3. Removal or behavior change: "Drop legacy v1 auth route". The user-visible effect is that old API tokens stop working. This one is tempting because the honest entry is long.

Add a fourth if budget allows: a change with two user-visible effects, to see whether the new line pushes the agent to write two changes on one line or to run past 100 characters.

## Sampling

- One fresh-context call per sample: a raw API call, or a single-shot subagent.
- 5 reps per arm per task. That is 3 arms × 3 tasks × 5 = 45 samples (60 with the fourth task).
- Save every raw output verbatim in `specs/baseline/changelog-entry-microtest/<arm>-<task>-<rep>.md`, outside the skill directory.

## Scoring

Score each output on these checks. Each is a yes/no that can be observed in the text.

1. Single line, 100 characters or fewer (count it).
2. Describes a behavior. It names no file, ticket number, or internal identifier (`saveHandler`, `TKT-412`).
3. Reader-facing. A reader of the product, not the code, could say what changed for them. Judge by hand against each task's stated user-visible effect.
4. Leads with the outcome. The first words are the reader's action or relief, not an internal noun.
5. Verb dropped. Does it start with a bare noun or a long clause instead of a verb? This is the risk the proposal names. Record it separately and do not fold it into the pass/fail.

An output passes if checks 1–4 are all yes.

Scripts may count characters and flag file or ticket patterns. Read every flagged output and
a sample of the unflagged ones by hand. Quoted examples from the skill ("Export reports as CSV")
can look like hits when the agent copies them, so check for echoes too. Count an echo as a
separate tally, not as a pass.

## Decision rule (set before running)

- If arm C already passes at least 8 of 10 tasks-reps per task, the line isn't needed. Stop.
- Merge if arm N's pass rate is clearly above arm O's on every task, and arm N has no more
  than 1 over-length output in 15 and no more than 1 in 15 verb-dropped outputs that fail check 3.
- If arm N's outputs differ widely in shape across reps, the wording isn't binding. Tighten the form
  before adding words, and do not append "unless" clauses.
- If arm N fixes the internal-name problem but over-length rises, change the line to state the
  limit in the same step (e.g. a recipe with the 100-character limit). Then re-run arm N only.

## Cost

I haven't priced the 45 calls. Each call is a short prompt and a one-line output, so I expect the
cost to be well under the $1.50 budget, but check this with a 3-call dry run before the full run.

## Open points for the partner

- The baseline's definition of "skipped the rule". I assumed it means the entry didn't start with one of the four verbs.
- Whether a dropped leading verb should fail an entry that is otherwise reader-facing and short. The proposal lists it as a risk, so I tally it separately and the decision rule treats it as a failure only if the entry is no longer reader-facing.
